Subject: Evaluation window + MAP ask for MSA/DPA sequencing

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the model variance controls. We want to move toward a short pilot so procurement/legal can validate compliance controls. Before we lock dates, can you send a simple mutual action plan that maps evaluation milestones to the legal/contract steps (MSA, DPA, order form)?

Specifically: can you outline the critical path for us including:
- SOC2 evidence or equivalent artifacts needed for legal review
- Typical redline turn times for MSA vs DPA (we have a few addenda to confirm)
- Order-form info required to price the pilot and sign at the end of the evaluation

We have a 3-week evaluation window in mind starting Aug 7; procurement would like to see whether the contract-level items (DPA & order form) can be executed within the same 3-week sprint or if we should plan a separate ticket.

Attaching our internal evaluation checklist (for context).

Alyssa

Subject: Re: Evaluation window + MAP ask for MSA/DPA sequencing

Hi Alyssa — appreciate the clarity and the checklist. I put together a compact MAP that maps evaluation milestones to procurement/legal gates and an order-form handoff. High level below — I'll attach a one-page MAP (MAP-draft.xlsx) for you to share with stakeholders.

High-level MAP (proposed, conservative):
1) Week 0 (prep): NDA existing, SOC2 evidence link requested from us (we include a redacted controls summary).
2) Week 1 (pilot start): Technical evaluation kickoff; we run integration tests and baseline performance profiles.
3) Week 2 (mid-eval): Customer shares evaluation feedback; procurement begins DPA review in parallel with legal reviewing SOC2 evidence.
4) Week 3 (close of eval): Technical signoff or list of acceptance items. Order-form draft circulated for pricing + billing terms.
5) Week 4–6 (contract cadence): Typical legal turnaround for MSA+DPA redlines is 7–14 business days each if there are standard, minor edits. If Novena needs extensive DPA addenda or third-party clauses, add another 1–2 weeks.

Fast-lane option: If Novena can accept our standard DPA (we can surface the small optional clauses ahead of time) and if procurement provides a single consolidated redline set, we can target signature within 2 weeks of eval close (i.e., 5 weeks total).

Decision items for Novena that affect the timeline:
- SOC2 evidence vs. attestation: is a controls summary sufficient or do you need the full SOC2 report?
- Any bespoke data residency / retention clauses beyond our standard DPA?

Proposed next step: quick 30m alignment call with procurement + legal (we're suggesting Mon/Tue next week) to agree MAP and confirm whether to run pilot within the same sprint or split into eval + contract sprint.

I've attached the MAP-draft.xlsx and a redline template for your legal team to use — that should speed review.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP draft — quick legal/procurement sync (RDW-4582)

Laura / Karthik — forwarding Alyssa's note and my MAP draft. Novena wants to start a 3-week evaluation the week of Aug 7 and is asking whether contract-level items (DPA + order form) can be executed inside that window or should be treated as a follow-on sprint.

Key asks for legal/procurement:
- Can we accept Novena's proposed DPA addendum wording? If not, how many business days to produce a counter-redline?
- If we surface our standard DPA + the three optional clauses in redline_template.docx, could they be treated as "accept unless changed" to speed signature?
- Any non-standard procurement requests that typically add time (e.g., escrow, independent audits, specific indemnity changes)?

I'm proposing two possible paths:
A) Conservative: eval = tech only; contract sprint after eval (adds ~2 weeks)
B) Accelerate: run procurement in parallel and try to close during the eval (needs legal priority + SOC2 attestation flagged as "sufficient")

If we can do B and legal estimates ~7 business days to finalize MSA+DPA, we can stay within Novena's desired timeline and possibly convert pilot to paid capacity quickly.

Please reply with: 1) realistic turn times in business days for MSA and DPA redline cycles, 2) any known blockers for RDW-4582, and 3) whether you want me to schedule a three-way call with Novena's legal this week.
